title.es: El estilo nominal en el trabajo

es: Reconocer y formar sustantivos abstractos a partir de verbos y adjetivos (decide → decision, kind → kindness) y leerlos en un texto breve.

teaching.en: The committee's refusal to publish the accounts damaged public trust and raised serious doubts about its transparency.
teaching.es: La negativa del comité a publicar las cuentas dañó la confianza pública y suscitó serias dudas sobre su transparencia.
teaching.explanationEs: refuse → refusal y transparent → transparency: la nominalización deja la idea como protagonista y oculta quién se negó.
segments: The committee's refusal to publish the accounts damaged public
trust and raised serious doubts about its transparency.
teaching.audioText: The committee's refusal to publish the accounts damaged public trust and raised serious doubts about its transparency.

teaching.en: It took the board three long meetings to reach a decision on the development of the old harbour.
teaching.es: El consejo necesitó tres reuniones largas para tomar una decisión sobre el desarrollo del antiguo puerto.
teaching.explanationEs: reach a decision es la colocación natural (no «take»); develop → development añade -ment al verbo.
segments: It took the board three long meetings to reach
a decision on the development of the old harbour.
teaching.audioText: It took the board three long meetings to reach a decision on the development of the old harbour.

teaching.en: Customers rarely praise reliability in a supplier, yet a single failure to deliver on time can cost a firm its best contract.
teaching.es: Los clientes rara vez elogian la fiabilidad de un proveedor, pero un solo fallo en la entrega puede costarle a una empresa su mejor contrato.
teaching.explanationEs: reliable → reliability (-able → -ability) y fail → failure (-ure): failure to + verbo nombra lo que no se logró.
segments: Customers rarely praise reliability in a supplier, yet a single failure
to deliver on time can cost a firm its best contract.
teaching.audioText: Customers rarely praise reliability in a supplier, yet a single failure to deliver on time can cost a firm its best contract.

teaching.en: On arrival, visitors noticed a marked improvement in the signage, and several remarked on the kindness of the volunteers.
teaching.es: A su llegada, los visitantes notaron una mejora notable en la señalización, y varios comentaron la amabilidad de los voluntarios.
teaching.explanationEs: on arrival es una fórmula fija de informes; kind → kindness y improve → improvement (-ness, -ment).
segments: On arrival, visitors noticed a marked improvement in the signage,
and several remarked on the kindness of the volunteers.
teaching.audioText: On arrival, visitors noticed a marked improvement in the signage, and several remarked on the kindness of the volunteers.

teaching.en: Sustained growth rests on reliability rather than on dramatic breakthroughs, and the difference usually shows after a decade.
teaching.es: El crecimiento sostenido se apoya en la fiabilidad más que en avances espectaculares, y la diferencia suele verse después de una década.
teaching.explanationEs: grow → growth tiene forma propia; differ → difference usa -ence: cada pareja se aprende entera.
segments: Sustained growth rests on reliability rather than on dramatic
breakthroughs, and the difference usually shows after a decade.
teaching.audioText: Sustained growth rests on reliability rather than on dramatic breakthroughs, and the difference usually shows after a decade.

teaching.en: The late departure of the delegation caused little disruption, but the difference in tone between the two speeches was striking.
teaching.es: La salida tardía de la delegación causó pocas molestias, pero la diferencia de tono entre los dos discursos fue llamativa.
teaching.explanationEs: depart → departure (-ure); el sustantivo puede llevar adjetivo delante (late departure) y of después.
segments: The late departure of the delegation caused little disruption, but
the difference in tone between the two speeches was striking.
teaching.audioText: The late departure of the delegation caused little disruption, but the difference in tone between the two speeches was striking.

prompt.es: Elige el sustantivo que falta en la noticia sobre la biblioteca.

choices.text: decision
deciding
decisive

feedback.es: Después de The hace falta un sustantivo abstracto: decision (de decide), que lleva to close como complemento.

hint.es: Después de The y antes de to close va un sustantivo, no un verbo ni un adjetivo.

origin.text: The ___ to close the library surprised the whole town, because the council had promised only a month earlier to keep it open.

prompt.es: Completa: «La llegada del nuevo profesor cambió el ambiente de la clase.»

feedback.es: Arrival es el sustantivo de arrive (-e → -al) y puede ser el sujeto del verbo changed.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de arrive; el verbo solo no funciona después de The.

origin.text: The ___ of the new teacher changed the mood of the class; pupils who had barely spoken for weeks began to ask questions.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El crecimiento constante del pueblo sorprendió incluso al ayuntamiento local.»

answer.text: The steady growth of the village surprised even the local council

feedback.es: El grupo nominal The steady growth of the village es el sujeto y va antes del verbo surprised.

hint.es: El sujeto es un grupo nominal largo; el verbo surprised va después de village.

prompt.es: Une cada pareja verbo o adjetivo → sustantivo con su significado.

feedback.es: Cada pareja cambia de forma de manera distinta: -ency, -ure, -al y -ence; conviene aprenderlas enteras.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige qué salió bien tras el cambio de transportista.

choices.text: The first supplier has become the firm's most reliable partner.
The new carrier has not been late with a single parcel.
Sales have recovered fully after the change of carrier.

feedback.es: Reliability of the new carrier significa que todos los paquetes llegan a tiempo; el crecimiento, en cambio, se ha frenado.

origin.audio: The regional manager's report was blunt. Since the decision to change carrier, the company's growth has slowed for two quarters, and the failure of the first supplier to meet its deadlines did not help. Yet the reliability of the new carrier has been striking: not one parcel has arrived late since the departure of the old driver in October. The manager added that the refusal of the landlord to negotiate had finally forced the company to make a change it should have made years ago.

prompt.es: Completa cada frase con el sustantivo de la palabra entre paréntesis.

feedback.es: Agree, able y safe forman agreement, ability y safety: -ment, -ity y -ty.

sentences: The two sides finally signed an ___ after a month of talks. (agree)
Nobody doubted her ___ as a team leader. (able)
The ___ of the children must always come first. (safe)

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el autor del correo sobre el cambio de oficina?

choices.text: That the landlord alone is to blame and the team should complain.
That speed matters more than honesty in carrying out the plan.
That the old office had been a mistake from the very beginning.
That the move was expected and should not be read as a loss.

feedback.es: El autor recuerda que los problemas se veían desde la primavera y pide no vivir la salida como una derrota: la mudanza era previsible.

origin.text: Dear all, the landlord's refusal to accept a new contract leaves us with little choice, but I would not call the decision sudden: the failure of our negotiations has been visible since spring. I ask only that we measure the development of the plan by its transparency, not by its speed, and that nobody treat the departure from the old office as a defeat.

prompt.es: Convierte cada palabra en sustantivo para completar las frases.

feedback.es: Patient, explain, pay y honest dan patience, explanation, payment y honesty: cada pareja tiene su terminación.

sentences: Her ___ with difficult customers was respected by the whole team. (patient)
Nobody understood the ___ offered for the long delay. (explain)
The ___ of the invoice is due before the end of the month. (pay)
His ___ about the mistake won him the manager's respect. (honest)

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué actitud muestra la presentadora ante su error.

choices.text: She accepts responsibility and sees the lesson in the failure.
She regrets the failure but mainly blames difficult market conditions.
She feels the failure was unfair and would repeat the same plan.

feedback.es: No culpa al mercado ni a sus socios: asume su propia negativa a escuchar las advertencias y valora la lección del fracaso.

origin.audio: In the final episode, the host admits that her confidence was a mistake. The growth she predicted never came, and the failure, she says, taught her more than any success. She does not blame the market or her partners; she blames her own refusal to listen to the early warnings that her adviser kept repeating.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La salida repentina del director causó bastante preocupación entre el personal.»

answer.text: The sudden departure of the manager caused serious concern among the staff

feedback.es: El sujeto es el grupo nominal The sudden departure of the manager; caused es el verbo principal.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento de la reunión y elige con qué intención habla la directora.

choices.text: To announce that the delivery problems have now been solved.
To urge the team to stay cautious and report problems early.
To blame the two drivers who decided to leave the firm.

feedback.es: Reconoce la mejora pero advierte de que no es crecimiento sostenido y pide avisar pronto: busca prudencia, no celebración ni reproches.

origin.audio: Let me be honest about the figures. The improvement in our delivery times is real, but I would not celebrate yet. A single week of good results is not sustained growth, and the departure of two experienced drivers could ruin everything within a month. So my request is simple: keep the reliability of the past month, and tell me early if anything starts to go wrong.

prompt.es: Completa: «La auditoría halló una mejora notable en las cuentas de la empresa.»

feedback.es: Marked improvement es la colocación formal para una mejora claramente visible.

origin.text: The audit found a ___ improvement in the firm's accounts: costs were lower, errors had fallen and the reports were finally on time.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito usa la autora tantas nominalizaciones en el informe?

choices.text: To show that the board revealed the figures to everyone involved.
To blame the two directors who had left for the whole crisis.
To keep an impersonal tone that leaves the responsible people unnamed.
To praise the investigation for naming those who were responsible.

feedback.es: Refusal, departure y failure convierten acciones en cosas: el texto suena objetivo y nunca dice quién decidió, salió o falló.

origin.text: The refusal of the board to reveal the figures led to a loss of confidence. The departure of two directors followed, and the failure of the investigation to name anyone has left the question of responsibility open.

es: Construir grupos nominales largos con la preposición fija de cada nominalización (a reduction in, demand for, a solution to) y usar due to y as a result of delante de un grupo nominal.

teaching.en: The council reported a sharp reduction in air pollution last year, and a steep increase in the number of cyclists seems to explain it.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento informó de una fuerte reducción de la contaminación del aire el año pasado, y un aumento pronunciado del número de ciclistas parece explicarla.
teaching.explanationEs: reduction + in: in introduce lo que disminuye; increase in + lo que sube (con cifra: an increase of ten per cent).
segments: The council reported a sharp reduction in air pollution last year, and
a steep increase in the number of cyclists seems to explain it.
teaching.audioText: The council reported a sharp reduction in air pollution last year, and a steep increase in the number of cyclists seems to explain it.

teaching.en: A lack of qualified drivers forced the company to cut evening services, even though demand for them had never been higher.
teaching.es: La falta de conductores calificados obligó a la empresa a recortar los servicios de la tarde, aunque la demanda de estos nunca había sido mayor.
teaching.explanationEs: lack of y demand for: la preposición no siempre coincide con el español («demanda de» = demand for).
segments: A lack of qualified drivers forced the company to cut evening
services, even though demand for them had never been higher.
teaching.audioText: A lack of qualified drivers forced the company to cut evening services, even though demand for them had never been higher.

teaching.en: The authorities need a solution to the flooding, because the storm did serious damage to the bridges and to several roads.
teaching.es: Las autoridades necesitan una solución a las inundaciones, porque la tormenta causó graves daños en los puentes y en varias carreteras.
teaching.explanationEs: a solution to y damage to: en inglés estos nombres se construyen con to, no con of.
segments: The authorities need a solution to the flooding, because the storm
did serious damage to the bridges and to several roads.
teaching.audioText: The authorities need a solution to the flooding, because the storm did serious damage to the bridges and to several roads.

teaching.en: In response to the complaints, the manager promised that the damage to the firm's reputation would be repaired, but a knock-on effect on delivery times seems likely.
teaching.es: En respuesta a las quejas, el director prometió que se repararía el daño a la reputación de la empresa, pero parece probable un efecto en cadena sobre los plazos de entrega.
teaching.explanationEs: in response to + grupo nominal; a knock-on effect on: el efecto indirecto de algo que ya ocurrió.
segments: In response to the complaints, the manager promised that the damage to the firm's
reputation would be repaired, but a knock-on effect on delivery times seems likely.
teaching.audioText: In response to the complaints, the manager promised that the damage to the firm's reputation would be repaired, but a knock-on effect on delivery times seems likely.

teaching.en: Due to the heavy snow the match was moved, and owing to a shortfall in ticket sales the club blamed a lack of public interest.
teaching.es: Debido a la fuerte nevada el partido se aplazó, y a causa de un déficit en la venta de entradas el club culpó a la falta de interés del público.
teaching.explanationEs: due to y owing to van delante de un grupo nominal (the heavy snow), nunca de una oración con verbo conjugado.
segments: Due to the heavy snow the match was moved, and owing to a
shortfall in ticket sales the club blamed a lack of public interest.
teaching.audioText: Due to the heavy snow the match was moved, and owing to a shortfall in ticket sales the club blamed a lack of public interest.

teaching.en: As a result of the delay, many fans left early, and the effect on local shops was a reduction in takings that nobody had predicted.
teaching.es: Como resultado del retraso, muchos aficionados se marcharon temprano, y el efecto en los comercios locales fue una reducción de la recaudación que nadie había previsto.
teaching.explanationEs: as a result of + grupo nominal (the delay); effect on + quién o qué resulta afectado.
segments: As a result of the delay, many fans left early, and the effect
on local shops was a reduction in takings that nobody had predicted.
teaching.audioText: As a result of the delay, many fans left early, and the effect on local shops was a reduction in takings that nobody had predicted.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hubo una fuerte reducción del ruido en la zona.»

feedback.es: Reduction se une con in: a reduction in noise indica qué es lo que baja.

hint.es: Cada nombre lleva su preposición: aquí indica en qué cambió algo.

origin.text: Residents have welcomed the new road. There has been a sharp reduction ___ noise in the area, and the fact that heavy lorries now use the ring road is the main reason.

prompt.es: Elige el grupo nominal correcto para «falta de agua» en el texto.

choices.text: a lack for water
a lack of water
a lack in water

feedback.es: Lack va siempre con of: a lack of water, igual que a lack of time.

hint.es: Es la preposición más frecuente para unir dos nombres en inglés.

origin.text: The village had no rain for three months. By August the wells were almost empty, and everybody in the valley was talking about ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por un déficit de financiación, el museo cerró dos salas.»

answer.text: Owing to a shortfall in funding the museum closed two galleries
accepted: Owing to a shortfall in funding the museum closed two galleries
The museum closed two galleries owing to a shortfall in funding
Owing to a shortfall in funding, the museum closed two galleries

feedback.es: Owing to va delante del grupo nominal a shortfall in funding y la oración principal sigue después.

hint.es: Empieza con Owing to y un grupo nominal; después viene la oración principal.

prompt.es: Completa cada grupo nominal con la preposición fija.

feedback.es: Demand for, damage to, response to y effect on son combinaciones fijas que no siempre coinciden con el español.

sentences: The demand ___ electric bikes has grown sharply since the new law.
The storm caused serious damage ___ the roof of the old theatre.
Her response ___ the news was calm, almost cold.
The new rule had an unexpected effect ___ small shops.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia de radio y elige por qué se recortaron los trenes de la tarde.

choices.text: Evening services were reduced because few people use them.
Evening services were reduced because local companies complained.
Evening services were reduced because funding fell short.

feedback.es: El recorte se debe al déficit de financiación; que la demanda sea baja es lo que dice la empresa, no la causa que da la noticia.

origin.audio: Commuters will face longer journeys this winter. Owing to a shortfall in funding, the regional train company has cut its evening services, and in response to the cuts, local companies have complained of a knock-on effect on staff attendance: some workers now leave early to catch the last train, while others no longer come at all. The company insists that demand for late trains is low, but passengers say the lack of a reliable service is what keeps them away. A solution to the conflict now depends on the council.

prompt.es: Une cada grupo nominal con su equivalente en español.

pairs.es: un fuerte aumento de los alquileres
un efecto en cadena sobre los precios

feedback.es: Las preposiciones cambian respecto al español: in, on, to y in aparecen donde en español va «de» o «sobre».

pairs.es: un fuerte aumento de los alquileres
un efecto en cadena sobre los precios

prompt.es: Completa: «Debido a la fuerte nevada, el campo no se podía usar.»

feedback.es: Due to, owing to, because of y as a result of introducen un grupo nominal (the heavy snow), nunca un verbo conjugado.

origin.text: The match was called off at the last minute. ___ the heavy snow, the pitch was too wet to play on, and the club now faces a loss of ticket income.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la directora ante la queja de los viajeros?

choices.text: Understanding, but reluctant to promise any change.
Dismissive of the complaint, which she calls unfair.
Apologetic, and ready to bring the trains back at once.
Defensive, and sure that the demand is exaggerated.

feedback.es: Reconoce la dificultad y la demanda, pero se limita a decir que quizá haya una solución en primavera y no la promete.

origin.text: Thank you for your letter. I accept that the reduction in evening services has caused difficulty, and I do not question the demand for them. However, there was a shortfall in our budget, and the damage to our accounts left us no alternative. A solution to the problem may come next spring, but I cannot promise it.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige qué da a entender sobre la postura de la alcaldesa.

choices.text: She agrees that families now need urgent help from the state.
She doubts that the problem is as serious as the charities say.
She expects food prices to fall back to their old level soon.

feedback.es: Al afirmar que las cifras exageran el problema y que los salarios suben más que los precios, la alcaldesa pone en duda la gravedad que describen las organizaciones.

origin.audio: An increase of five per cent in food prices has had a serious effect on many families, and charities report a steep rise in requests for help. Yet the mayor insists that the figures exaggerate the problem, and claims that salaries have risen faster than prices.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un fuerte aumento de los alquileres afectó mucho a las tiendas pequeñas.»

answer.text: A steep increase in rents had a serious effect on small shops

feedback.es: El sujeto es A steep increase in rents; had a serious effect on introduce lo afectado.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el aviso sobre los sábados junto al mercado?

choices.text: That the market will close on Saturdays during the work.
That the shuttle bus will be free for all customers.
That the new car park may still prove too small.
That traders want the car park to be removed.

feedback.es: Si la demanda de espacios va a superar la oferta, el estacionamiento nuevo puede quedarse pequeño los sábados; el aviso no dice nada del mercado ni del precio del autobús.

origin.text: Notice: As a result of the building work, there is a reduction in parking near the market. Traders have welcomed the new car park, but they warn that the demand for spaces will be greater than the supply on Saturdays. The council hopes that a shuttle bus will provide a solution to the problem.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hay una gran demanda de clases de inglés en la ciudad.»

feedback.es: Demand for nombra el interés del público por algo; se une con for, no con of.

origin.text: There is a big ___ for English classes in the city, and several schools have had to open extra evening groups.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La falta de conductores tuvo un efecto en cadena en todo el sistema.»

answer.text: The lack of drivers had a knock-on effect on the whole system

feedback.es: The lack of drivers es el sujeto; a knock-on effect on the whole system nombra la consecuencia.

es: Desmontar frases densas con sustantivos abstractos: volver al verbo, recuperar quién hace qué y reformular con verbos claros.

teaching.en: The introduction of free lunches led to a steady rise in attendance, yet the report never says who took the decision.
teaching.es: La introducción de comidas gratuitas llevó a un aumento constante de la asistencia, pero el informe nunca dice quién tomó la decisión.
teaching.explanationEs: introduction y attendance esconden acciones (alguien introdujo, más alumnos asistieron) y el agente no aparece.
segments: The introduction of free lunches led to a steady rise in
attendance, yet the report never says who took the decision.
teaching.audioText: The introduction of free lunches led to a steady rise in attendance, yet the report never says who took the decision.

teaching.en: The closure of the clinic prompted residents to voice concerns, although the notice did not reveal who had ordered it.
teaching.es: El cierre de la clínica llevó a los vecinos a expresar sus preocupaciones, aunque el aviso no reveló quién lo había ordenado.
teaching.explanationEs: closure oculta al agente: alguien cerró la clínica. voice concerns es la colocación para expresar inquietudes en público.
segments: The closure of the clinic prompted residents to voice concerns,
although the notice did not reveal who had ordered it.
teaching.audioText: The closure of the clinic prompted residents to voice concerns, although the notice did not reveal who had ordered it.

teaching.en: Approval of the plan came only after the council agreed to launch an investigation into a serious complaint about safety.
teaching.es: La aprobación del plan llegó solo después de que el ayuntamiento aceptara abrir una investigación sobre una queja grave de seguridad.
teaching.explanationEs: approval, investigation y complaint vuelven a los verbos approve, investigate y complain; launch an investigation es la colocación habitual.
segments: Approval of the plan came only after the council agreed
to launch an investigation into a serious complaint about safety.
teaching.audioText: Approval of the plan came only after the council agreed to launch an investigation into a serious complaint about safety.

teaching.en: A decrease in complaints followed the publication of the results, which the press described as a victory for accountability.
teaching.es: Una disminución de las quejas siguió a la publicación de los resultados, que la prensa describió como una victoria de la rendición de cuentas.
teaching.explanationEs: decrease y publication esconden acciones; accountability nombra quién debe responder de lo que hizo.
segments: A decrease in complaints followed the publication of the results,
which the press described as a victory for accountability.
teaching.audioText: A decrease in complaints followed the publication of the results, which the press described as a victory for accountability.

teaching.en: To unpack a dense sentence, find the abstract noun, return to its verb and ask who performed the action.
teaching.es: Para desmontar una frase densa, localiza el sustantivo abstracto, vuelve a su verbo y pregunta quién realizó la acción.
teaching.explanationEs: unpack resume el método: sustantivo → verbo → agente. Si el texto no dice quién actúa, no lo inventes.
segments: To unpack a dense sentence, find the abstract noun, return
to its verb and ask who performed the action.
teaching.audioText: To unpack a dense sentence, find the abstract noun, return to its verb and ask who performed the action.

teaching.en: The council closed the clinic after a heated discussion, so residents demanded accountability for a decision nobody had explained.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento cerró la clínica tras una discusión acalorada, así que los vecinos exigieron rendición de cuentas por una decisión que nadie había explicado.
teaching.explanationEs: Versión con verbos: ahora aparecen el agente (the council) y la acción (closed the clinic).
segments: The council closed the clinic after a heated discussion, so
residents demanded accountability for a decision nobody had explained.
teaching.audioText: The council closed the clinic after a heated discussion, so residents demanded accountability for a decision nobody had explained.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con verbos de la frase sobre las comidas gratuitas.

choices.text: The school introduced free lunches because more pupils had attended.
More pupils attended, so the school introduced free lunches.
The school introduced free lunches, and more pupils began to attend.

feedback.es: Introduction vuelve a introduced, attendance a attend, y el orden causa-efecto se conserva: primero las comidas, después más asistencia.

hint.es: Busca el verbo escondido en introduction y en attendance, y respeta qué ocurrió primero.

origin.text: The school's introduction of free lunches led to a rise in attendance, but the report never states who paid for them.

prompt.es: Completa la versión verbal: «El ayuntamiento aprobó el plan tras semanas de debate.»

feedback.es: Approval esconde el verbo approve; en pasado es approved y the council es el agente.

hint.es: Vuelve del sustantivo approval al verbo, en pasado.

origin.text: Approval of the plan came only after weeks of debate. In other words, the council ___ the plan after weeks of debate, but the report does not say who proposed it.

prompt.es: Elige el verbo que esconde el sustantivo publication en la frase.

choices.text: publish
public
publicly

feedback.es: Publication viene del verbo publish: alguien publicó los resultados, aunque la frase no diga quién.

hint.es: Quita la terminación del sustantivo y piensa en la acción.

origin.text: A decrease in complaints followed the publication of the results, which the press described as a victory for accountability.

prompt.es: Completa cada versión verbal con el verbo escondido en el sustantivo.

feedback.es: Closure, investigation y decrease vuelven a closed, investigated y decreased.

sentences: The closure of the shop upset many regulars. → The owner ___ the shop, and many regulars were upset.
The investigation of the fire took a week. → The police ___ the fire for a week.
The decrease in noise pleased the residents. → The noise ___, and the residents were pleased.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige qué dato no se puede saber con lo que dice.

choices.text: Whether the traders complained about the charges.
Who was responsible for approving the scheme.
Whether the figures showed a fall in visitors.

feedback.es: El informe dice que nadie ha explicado quién fue el responsable: si el texto no nombra al agente, no se puede inventar.

origin.audio: The introduction of the new parking charges led to a steady decrease in attendance at the market. Traders voiced concerns, and the publication of the council's figures, which showed a fall of twenty per cent, only increased the anger. Approval of the scheme had been given after a short discussion, and nobody has yet explained who was responsible. The council's refusal to reconsider has raised questions about accountability, and local businesses are now calling for an investigation into the decision.

prompt.es: Une cada frase densa con la acción que esconde, en español.

feedback.es: Cada sustantivo esconde un verbo: introduce, publish, approve y attend.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el autor al describir el cierre de la planta con tantos sustantivos?

choices.text: That the closure was a direct result of the new safety rules.
That the police delayed the approval of the new rules.
That the closure is presented as something that happened, not as a choice.
That the author wants readers to know who raised the alarm.

feedback.es: Con closure, approval y publication y sin agentes, el cierre parece un hecho inevitable y no una decisión de alguien; el texto no dice que las normas lo causaran.

origin.text: The publication of the findings led to an investigation and, later, the approval of new safety rules. At no point does the report say who first raised the alarm, and the closure of the plant is described throughout as a necessary step.

prompt.es: Rehaz cada frase con el verbo que se esconde en su sustantivo.

feedback.es: Introduction, complaint y refusal vuelven a introduced, complained y refused.

sentences: The introduction of a new timetable divided the staff. → The firm ___ a new timetable, and the staff were divided.
The complaint of the parents was heard at the meeting. → The parents ___ at the meeting.

answer.text: The construction of the new neighbourhood library was delayed by two years, owing to a shortage of skilled workers in the region. This delay gave rise to anger among local families and to a wave of complaints addressed to the council. In the wake of these problems, a sharp rise in the price of materials, which stemmed from the suppliers' failure to deliver on time, led to a cost overrun, since the council also had to pay the workers for extra months. The newspaper's questions prompted the council to promise an investigation into the lack of planning. The outcome, however, has been positive: the opening of the library in September has brought about a steady increase in visitors, now above a thousand a week, and a marked improvement in the children's reading. origin.text: Two years ago the council decided to build a new library in our neighbourhood, and everybody was pleased. However, the builders were late because there were not enough skilled workers in the region, so the work fell behind schedule. As a result, the library opened two years late, and many families were angry and sent letters of complaint to the council. While they waited, the price of materials rose sharply, because the suppliers could not deliver on time, and the council had to pay the workers for extra months. In the wake of these problems, the newspaper asked why nobody had planned for the risk, and the council promised that it would investigate the matter. Finally, the library opened in September. The council had spent much more money than it had planned, but the result was good: every week more than a thousand people visit, and the children read much more than before. Looking back, the director says that the delay taught the council to plan more carefully, and that the families who complained deserve thanks, because their letters made the council act.

answer.text: The fast expansion of community gardens in European cities has led to a marked reduction in stress and in food costs for many families, according to a growing body of evidence. Researchers who followed four hundred gardeners for two years also found that participation brings neighbours together and encourages them to share tools, seeds and advice. However, this expansion is limited by a shortage of vacant land, and councils disagree about the allocation of plots: some would give priority to schools, others to older residents, and a few to whoever has waited longest. One researcher warns that the lack of a fair system could turn a popular project into a source of anger. A key finding of the study is that gardens work well when residents help to make the rules. The next step, therefore, is a transparent system for the allocation of land that every neighbour can understand and trust. In short, the gardens offer clear social and health benefits, but only a fair allocation of land will allow them to keep growing.

origin.text: Community gardens are spreading fast through European cities. In the last ten years, thousands of neighbours have started to grow vegetables together on small plots of public land, and a growing body of evidence suggests that the benefits go well beyond fresh food. Researchers who followed four hundred gardeners for two years report a marked reduction in stress, and many families say that they now spend less money on food. Participation has also brought people together: in several districts, neighbours who had never spoken now share tools, seeds and advice. However, the expansion has a clear limit. Vacant land is scarce, and councils disagree about the allocation of the plots. Some want to give them first to schools, others to older residents, and a few argue that the places should go to whoever has waited longest. One researcher warns that the lack of a fair system could turn a popular project into a source of anger. A key finding of the study is that gardens work well when residents help to make the rules.
